92 THE SAVOY MALE AND FEMALE COLLEGE

E. L. Strother appears instead of C. E. Phillips as Local Editor for the December and subsequent issues. For the spring of 1886, W. J. Bill Suddith, who was apparently a member of the class, looking very wise and dignified, ran the business department of the paper very efficiently. Other college representatives were J. D. Warren, and Miss Janie Lucy; and by the June issue, Misses Maud Montgomery and Julia Hunt had come in as Junior and Local Editors, respectively. The coeducational trend had at last made itself felt; and coeds held these positions of responsibility with the men on the staff.

In the fall of 1886, the only available number for that collegiate year, W. J. Hollingsworth appears as Business Manager and Drs. J. Reynolds, W. E. Pierce, A. C. Jones and J. M. Conway as editors.

NATURE OF CONTENT—A typical issue of the Messenger was well calculated to serve the purpose of being "the organ and representative of Savoy College in the surrounding community." Subsequently an 1885-1886 number states:

The Platonian Messenger is one of the largest and best College papers in the State. We spare no effort to make it creditable in all its hidousneso[?], but shall ever strive to excel in the noble qualities characteristic of a College paper that is worth reading.

Again, in the next month's issue, referring to its purpose, it better explained, from the students' viewpoint, that:

It is the aim of this paper to be everything to all men. Among its members we have students of music, those who have prepared for it and will try to have an important contribution; and also in the columns of the paper we have stories of importance.
